functionalJourney.title: Restore focus after closing a real dialog

plan.root_cause: The previouslyFocused variable can be null when getActiveEl() returns null (no focused element). The Safari fallback only updates previouslyFocused when its tagName is 'BODY', leaving it null, so hide() cannot restore focus to the opener.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the condition in the show() method to treat a null previouslyFocused as needing the fallback to event.target, ensuring a valid reference to the opener is stored before the dialog is opened.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Focus returns to the opener after closing the dialog with Escape, meeting WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.3 Focus Order, and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape after opening the dialog via Enter returns focus to the opener button.
Verify that clicking the opener and pressing Escape also returns focus to the opener.
Ensure the existing Safari workaround for body-focused clicks continues to function correctly.

plan.root_cause: When opening the dialog via keyboard (Enter on the opener button), getActiveEl() can return null if no element is focused. The Safari workaround only updates previouslyFocused when it's the BODY element, leaving it null. Consequently, hide() cannot restore focus to the opener because previouslyFocused?.focus?.() is a no-op.
plan.repair_strategy: Expand the fallback condition in show() to also trigger when previouslyFocused is null, not just when it's BODY. This ensures the click event target (the opener) is stored as the focus restoration target.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape after opening the dialog via Enter returns focus to the opener button, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: If event.target is not the opener (e.g., nested element), focus may restore to an unexpected element.
The fallback could capture an incorrect target if show() is called from a non-click context.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape after opening the dialog via Enter returns focus to the opener button.
Verify that clicking the opener and pressing Escape also returns focus to the opener.
Ensure the existing Safari workaround for body-focused clicks continues to function correctly.

plan.root_cause: The Safari workaround only restores the click target as the previously focused element when the active element is the BODY, but for keyboard activation the active element is the opener button, so the workaround does not trigger. However, the opener button should be the focus restoration target for both keyboard and mouse activation.
plan.repair_strategy: Expand the condition to capture the click event target for all click events (including keyboard-synthesized clicks), ensuring the element that triggered the dialog is stored as the focus restoration target.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape after opening the dialog via Enter returns focus to the opener button, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: If show() is called programmatically without a click event, getActiveEl() is used which may not be the intended opener.
If the click target is not focusable (e.g., a non-interactive element), focus restoration may fail.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape after opening the dialog via Enter returns focus to the opener button.
Verify that clicking the opener and pressing Escape also returns focus to the opener.
Ensure the existing Safari workaround for body-focused clicks continues to function correctly.
